mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDPC1 indicates strong economic demand, leading to higher S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are expected to improve.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in UNRATE below 4% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and equity prices.
failure_condition: UNRATE falls below 4% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: Low FEDFUNDS combined with low UNRATE indicates a supportive monetary policy and strong labor market, leading to positive S&P returns.
failure_condition: Both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE are low, but S&P 500 returns are negative over 20 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary easing cycle, low FEDFUNDS reduces borrowing costs, increasing equity valuations and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS is low but S&P 500 returns are not significantly higher during easing periods.

mechanism_narrative: Stable CPIAUCSL indicates controlled inflation, leading to positive equity returns as real interest rates remain favorable.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL is stable but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in INDPRO above 105 indicates strong industrial production, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO exceeds 105 but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing PAYEMS and RSAFS indicate strong employment and retail sales, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Both PAYEMS and RSAFS increase but S&P 500 returns are negative over 20 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising HOUST indicates housing market strength, signaling continued economic growth and positive S&P returns.
failure_condition: HOUST rises but S&P 500 returns are not significantly higher during late-cycle periods.
